explanation: Its name comes from helios, Greek for the Sun, where its spectral line was first seen in 1868. On Earth, William Ramsay found it in a uranium mineral in 1895.

claims.text: Helium was detected in the Sun's spectrum in 1868, decades before it was isolated on Earth in 1895.
The spectral line that revealed helium was first seen in sunlight in 1868, during a solar eclipse.
The name helium comes from helios, the Greek word for the Sun.
William Ramsay isolated helium on Earth in 1895, from a uranium mineral called cleveite.
